Welcome to Trevelyan Middle School
Trevelyan Middle School is a welcoming, inclusive learning community where pupils aged 9–13 are supported to grow academically, socially and personally during these important middle years. Guided by our ethos to inspire, challenge and grow, we are proud of a school that combines high expectations with care, curiosity and a strong sense of belonging.
At Trevelyan, people are at the heart of everything we do. We believe pupils thrive when they feel safe, known and valued, and when learning is ambitious, engaging and connected to the real world. Our curriculum is designed to nurture resilience, independence and social responsibility, while encouraging pupils to think critically and develop confidence in who they are and what they can achieve.
I am proud to be joining Trevelyan as Headteacher and see my role as building thoughtfully on the school’s many strengths. Trevelyan has a distinctive character and strong foundations, and my priority is to listen, learn and work closely with pupils, staff and families to ensure we continue to grow without losing what makes the school special. Any change will be carefully considered, purposeful and always rooted in the best interests of our pupils.
As part of the Pioneer Educational Trust, Trevelyan benefits from a collaborative culture, shared values and a strong commitment to inclusion and ethical leadership. We believe every child should be supported, celebrated and enabled to flourish.
Partnership with parents and carers is central to our success. I value open, honest communication and look forward to working closely with families to build trust and ensure every pupil feels supported to thrive, both in and beyond the classroom.
Trevelyan Middle School is a place where ambition is nurtured, individuality is respected and young people are encouraged to take education further. I look forward to the journey ahead and to being part of this special community.

pageCache.text:
Our Wraparound Care sessions promise to provide your children with a wide range of stimulating multi sports, creative activities, team games, themed arts and crafts and a whole host of imaginative things to make and do! Whether your child likes to play dodgeball, football, dance, tri-golf, basketball, or loves being creative and making different crafts, we guarantee we have something everyone will enjoy.
Please note that our Wraparound Care settings are only for children attending the school, who are in Year 5 to Year 8. Children will be returned to and collected from their class at the start/end of school registration and escorted to our club within the school building.
Please visit our website Wraparound Care – Get Active Sports to create an account and make your booking.
Bookings are available online until 9am on the day of the session. Please call our head office on 01344 860868 to book after this time.
Breakfast Club – 7.30am-8.25am – £8.55 per day (Breakfast included)
Short After School Club – 3.15pm-4.30pm – £9.25 per day (includes a snack)
Medium After School Club – 4.30pm-6pm – £10.75 per day (includes large snack)
Long After School Club – 3.15pm-6pm – £15.95 per day (includes a small and large snack)
Please note: Every Wednesday the After School club will run from 2.15pm until 6pm, £1 additional cost on each session.

PE and Sports Premium
At Trevelyan Middle School we are very proud of what we have on offer and our specialist provision; we recognise the significant contribution of PE to the health and well-being of all children. In addition, we believe that a varied PE curriculum and extra-curricular opportunities have a positive influence on the concentration, attitude and academic achievement of all children. We actively involve our Year 8 Sports Leaders in the organisation and activities offered to KS2 pupils.
The government has allocated additional funding on improving physical education (PE) and sport in primary school academic years. The funding is being jointly provided by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport. As a middle school we will receive funding for our key stage 2 pupils. We will use this allocated money for the benefit of all pupils regardless of their sporting ability and further extend our range on offer.

How Parents and Carers Evenings work at Trevelyan
Parents evenings take place once a year for each year group. This is a great opportunity for you to meet with teachers, discuss your child’s progress and see the school.
We seek to ensure that every parent gets an appointment for each of the three core subjects: English, Maths and Science. These appointments are made via MCAS. These appointments last five minutes and take place within our main school hall.
In addition, you may tour the school and meet with subject teachers for an informal conversation if you wish. Subject teachers will be based within their teaching rooms and pupils’ exercise books will be available for you to view. You do not need to make an appointment for these subjects and can attend as many or as few as you wish.
We strongly encourage you to bring your child to parents evening. As it concerns their education, we like to ensure they are part of the conversation.

They will run from 4pm – 7pm. Further information will be sent out to you nearer the time.

Safeguarding
Pioneer Educational Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people: the child or young person’s welfare is our overriding concern.
The schools within the Trust provide a caring, positive, stimulating and safe environment in which pupils can flourish academically and personally, and we ensure that pupils are enabled to develop socially, emotionally, physically and morally. As such, all adults, including volunteers, governors, trustees, visitors and temporary staff have an active part to play in protecting our pupils from harm.
The Trust has a Child Protection Policy in place. This policy can be found here.
Having the policy in place ensures that all members of the school community:
Sometimes we may need to share information and work in partnership with other agencies when there are concerns about a child or young person’s welfare. We will ensure that our concerns about our pupils are discussed with parents/carers first unless we have reason to believe that such a move would be contrary to the child or young person’s welfare.
If you have any concerns about a child or young person’s welfare, please record your concern and report this to one of the school’s safeguarding leads as soon as possible on the same day. It is important that you do not conduct your own investigation.
If your concerns relate to the behaviour or actions of a member of staff, then you should report this directly to the Head of School (or to the Chair of Governors if it relates to the Head of School).
Advice from the Department for Education on Radicalisation and Extremism
As children grow and become more independent, it is not unusual for them to take risks, explore new things and push boundaries. Teenage years are often a time when young people will be searching for answers to questions about identity, faith and belonging, as well as looking for adventure and excitement.
This can mean that they are particularly vulnerable to extremist groups, who may claim to offer answers, as well as identity and a strong social network. And because they know young people are vulnerable, extremist groups often target them using the internet and social media to spread their ideology. There have been a number of tragic examples where young people have been misled by extremist groups, with some travelling to Syria and others becoming involved in hate crimes against minority groups.
The purpose of this website is to provide practical advice and support to help all individuals with an interest in keeping children safe from the dangers of extremism. A website has been created by the Department for Education and the Home Office to offer us all guidance on how to spot potential issues. http://www.educateagainsthate.com/parents

Careers Advice
Trevelyan Middle School Careers Strategy 25-26
Trevelyan Middle School Careers Action Plan 25-26
Careers at Trevelyan
Our four values guide our approach to careers at Trevelyan. We are innovative, understanding that many of the jobs our pupils will undertake in the future do not currently exist; therefore, we nurture them to maintain an open mind while focusing on developing a broad range of employability skills. We teach our pupils resilience, encouraging healthy competition through our house system while promoting self-assessment and self-evaluation within the classroom, enabling them to find success and happiness no matter what the challenges of the future. We promote learners’ curiosity, ensuring they do not limit themselves into a fixed career path – but take joy about the infinite possibilities that exist. Finally, we instil in our young learners a sense of social responsibility, ensuring that no Trevelyan pupil leaves our school thinking just about what they can do for themselves, but instead thinking what they might contribute to wider world around them.
We use the Gatsby Benchmarks as a means to plan, implement and evaluate our careers provision. The Gatsby benchmarks are a framework of eight guidelines that define the best careers provision a school can offer.
Careers is an integral part of our Personal Development programme, which is primarily taught through a weekly PSHE lesson, but supported across and beyond the curriculum. You can find our full curriculum map for PSHE here.
Below, we articulate our careers provision across the eight Gatsby benchmarks:
1. A stable careers programme.
The six strands of our personal development programme, which is taught primarily through a weekly PSHE lesson, helps pupils develop the skills and aspirations they will require to hold fulfilling future careers.
Within the Society strand of our programme, pupils in Year 8 are taught about different career and educational pathways, including consideration of what jobs might exist in the future and growth industries. They are taught key employability skills and also their rights as employees. Prior to this, pupils in Year 7 are taught about financial management, including budgeting and tax.
This explicit careers teaching is supported from Year 5 upwards by a focus on how to maintain healthy relationships, a critical skill for the workplace. Through their study of our Diversity and Global strands, pupils are also continuously encouraged to widen their possibilities and overcome stereotypes that may inhibit what they believe they can do.
In addition, as of September 2023, KS3 pupils will be undertaking the Trevelyan Baccalaureate. One strand of this will be pupils undertaking the AQA Foundation Project Qualification. As well as giving pupils the experience of gaining a real qualification, it will also develop the key employability skills of communication, research and organisation.
2. Learning from career and labour market information
Our library contains a range of literature, appropriate to different age-groups, about career paths. Much of this is direct from career organisations or industry sectors. The library team work to offer displays within certain themes to promote this literature. Meanwhile, subjects will draw upon this literature to enhance areas of study within their subject area. We also maintain a list of useful online links on our website (see below).
3. Addressing the needs of each pupil
Our PSHE programme seeks to challenge stereotypical thinking across a range of areas, including careers. Across our wider curriculum, we seek to celebrate and usualise diversity at every opportunity.
In addition, we run targeted projects and interventions for pupils who we consider would benefit from developing particular employability skills. For example, we run a touch-typing course for pupils with particular SEND needs and we encourage identified pupils to take up our wide range of pupil leadership opportunities.
We maintain records of all the extra-curricular and enrichment activities each pupil receives, including that pertaining directly to careers. This is continuously monitored to ensure equal particular from differing groups of pupils.
4. Linking curriculum to learning in careers
All school subject areas provide opportunities for links with careers at different stages in pupils’ time at Trevelyan. All curriculum areas have formed a clear subject intent; these intents all revolve around making the subject relevant and meaningful to the child (including in the sense of careers).
There are many examples of how subject areas make these career links real to pupils. For example, within humanities, pupils undertake a series of trips where they are given the chance to “practice” career paths by taking part in practical activities (such as river investigations in Henley and historical investigations at Windsor castle). Within Physical Education, there is a focus on leadership within sport that is spread across the curriculum; in addition, enthusiastic pupils have the opportunity to undertake additional sports leadership training within Year 8. Within Performing Arts, pupils are not only provided with the opportunities to perform within the professionalised environment of a public show, but many pupils are also given the chance to undertake technical and creative crew roles.
5. Encounters with employers and employees
Our assembly programme seeks to bring in speakers from different career backgrounds for pupils to interact with. However, in Year 8, we also arrange for pupils to take part in a careers day, bringing together local community members who cover a range of career areas. Pupils use this experience to consider their own career path and the event leads into a reflection exercise they undertake within their PSHE lessons.
6. Experiences of workplaces
While this Gatsby benchmark refers directly to the work experience pupils usually undertake within KS4, we do still ensure we make provisions for workplace experiences at Trevelyan.
We have a wide range of pupil leadership opportunities for pupils of all years. This gives pupils a real opportunity to take responsibility and develop leadership skills. For example, we have our Pupil Leadership Team, our Heads and Deputy Heads of House, our Sports Leaders, our Pioneer Parliament and our Pupil Coaches.
As part of the aforementioned Trevelyan Baccalaureate, pupils will earn credits towards the Personal Development Programme strand. These credits will be earned, in part, through contributing work and taking responsibilities on a voluntary basis within their community.
7. Encounters with further and higher education
PSHE lessons within KS3 delve into different training routes required for different jobs, including encouraging pupils to undertake their own research into both higher and further education.
As part of our Year 8 careers day, we ensure coverage from both a post-16 school setting and a further education institution. We continue to seek and build partnership with a range of educational partners.
8. Personal guidance
Within Year 8, we seek to provide targeted personal guidance from a qualified careers advisor Year 8 pupils who would most benefit from this provision. This will be achieved in collaboration with local partners.
However, beyond dialogue with a qualified careers advisor, we seek to provide a range of opportunities for pupils to consider their personal goals and ambitions in dialogue with the staff members best placed to help them. This is achieved through our annual learning review day, which sees all pupils engage in a target-setting conversation with their parent/carer and form tutor.
As of September 2025 our careers lead is Ms Joy Mowat. She can be contacted via the school office.
